chat.text: I've been spending the afternoon immersed in this absolutely overwhelming, hyper-realistic painting of a suffocatingly desolate, infinite Arctic tundra. The artist captured the shrieking, violent wind with a terrifying precision—you can almost see the microscopic, needle-like frost crystals splintering in the air, smell the sterile, ozone-sharp caustic scent of deep freeze, and hear the deafening, guttural roar of a gale. The thick, suffocating, leaden oppressive grey of the monolithic winter sky feels heavy enough to crush you. It's so visceral that just looking at the razor-edged, crystalline shards of obsidian ice and the vast, frozen, wind-scoured plains of blinding, abrasive white makes my lungs burn with phantom frigid breaths and my skin tighten and crack, forcing me to pull my sweater tighter around me. When you picture a scene like that—that absolute, biting, bone-deep, soul-shattering cold—Describe the physical reaction you have when you picture a scene like that.
